    Getting started

    Start with the supplied reactor project to run a complete case and compare one operating change. The installation guide describes the four desktop downloads.

    Run the supplied project

    1. Download first-reactor.msproject (online) using GitHub's Download raw file button. Downloading needs internet; importing and running the saved project work offline.
    2. On the welcome screen, choose Import archived project and import the file into a writable project folder outside the application directory.
    3. Run its Baseline case. The first Compiled run may take several minutes. After Succeeded, open General → Requested plots → Outlet composition → Show.
    4. Duplicate Baseline, name the copy Lower flow, and change its Program → Inlet flow first ramp target (step 0) from 76.2568 to 60 mol/s. Run the copy to preserve the baseline results.
    5. Compare the two Outlet composition plots. Use Results… on the project screen to compare recorded quantities and export them to Excel.

    Continue with the GUI guide, or create a case from your own physical inputs below.

    Create your own case

    1. On the welcome screen, choose Create new project, give it a name, and select a local folder.
    2. Choose New Case on the project screen. The case starts as a draft with numerical defaults; it still needs your physical inputs.
    3. In Chemistry, select the gas and solid species and the required reactions.
    4. In Bed, enter the geometry and complete every material zone.
    5. In Program, set the initial feed and outlet pressure, then define timed steps or a repeating program with a suitable horizon.
    6. In General, review the solver, sampling, and recorded quantities. Select the reports needed for the plots and Excel analysis you want.
    7. Return to the project. When the case is Ready, choose its Run action.
    8. After Succeeded, open the case and use Show beside an available plot in General. Use Report to prepare an Excel export.

    Press F1 in the application for a short explanation of the screen or case tab you are using. The GUI guide provides the detailed workflows.

    Keep comparisons

    Each case keeps one latest run. To compare a changed case with a result you want to retain, duplicate the case, edit the copy, and run that copy. Results… on the project screen compares successful runs across cases.
